newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House backs U.N. slot for Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House backs U.N. slot for Taiwan.

text.p: The U.S. House approved a non-binding resolution on Tuesday supporting Taiwan's efforts to join the United Nations.
The measure, passed by voice vote, endorses a similar resolution adopted by the European Parliament on July 18.
The United States ended its official recognition of Taiwan when it reestabliship diplomatic relations with China two decades ago, but maintains unofficial ties with Taipai.
House International Relations Chairman Benjamin Gilman, R-New York, praised Taiwan as a democracy and a strong friend of the United States.

China regards Taiwan as a break-away province and protested strongly when the United States allowed Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui to make a private visit last year. Beijing is seen as certain to veto Taiwan's U.N. bid.
